title: Constructing and Implementing a Low-Cost On-Demand Morris Water Maze Platform

steps.title: Cut polycarbonate platform and base
steps.instruction: Using a saw, cut a 12 cm × 12 cm piece of polycarbonate for the platform and a 30 cm × 30 cm piece for the base.

steps.title: Attach mounting bracket to platform
steps.instruction: Center a mounting bracket on the platform, drill two 1/4 in holes through the plastic aligned with the bracket holes, then drill two shallow 1/2 in countersink holes on top of them for the screw heads. Secure the bracket with two hex flat‑head cap screws and stainless‑steel hex nuts.

steps.title: Attach mounting bracket to base
steps.instruction: Center a second mounting bracket on the base, drill two 1/4 in holes through the plastic aligned with the bracket, add two shallow 1/2 in countersink holes on the bottom of the base, and fasten with hex flat‑head cap screws and stainless‑steel hex nuts.

steps.title: Paint platform and hardware white
steps.instruction: Spray‑paint all surfaces of the platform, base, and screw caps white in a well‑ventilated area.

steps.title: Prepare underside for visual cue liner
steps.instruction: On the underside of the platform, drill four shallow pilot holes ~2 cm from each corner using a 1/16 in drill bit (do not drill through). Then screw a sheet‑metal screw into each hole so roughly half the screw protrudes.

steps.title: Secure platform to linear actuator
steps.instruction: Attach the platform bracket and the base bracket to the waterproof linear actuator (stroke length 10.16 cm = 4 in) using stainless‑steel hex bolts and nuts. Verify that the actuator’s remote control and power supply are connected.

steps.title: Add black drawer liner to platform
steps.instruction: Cut two pieces of black drawer liner to ~12 cm × 20 cm, fold them over the platform, and hook each piece onto the protruding sheet‑metal screws at the four corners.

steps.title: Seal tank seams and smooth surface
steps.instruction: Apply metal filler to all seams of the galvanized stock tank (1.82 m × 0.61 m) per the manufacturer’s instructions, then sand the filler smooth to create a uniform wall surface.

steps.title: Install drainage valve and wiring hole
steps.instruction: Drill a 3/4 in hole near the bottom of the tank (~2.5 cm up) and install the turn‑type hose‑bibb valve. Drill an additional ~25 mm hole near the base for the platform’s electrical wire.

steps.title: Create watertight wire entry with rubber stopper
steps.instruction: Use a standard rubber stopper for large test tubes (17 mm top diameter, 13 mm bottom diameter) with a single central hole. Slice a slit down the side of the stopper to the center hole, feed the wire through, and insert the stopper into the tank wall from the inside.

steps.title: Seal stopper and tank base with silicone
steps.instruction: Apply kitchen‑and‑bath silicone sealant around the rubber stopper and along any ridges on the tank bottom to prevent leaks.

steps.title: Paint interior top of tank
steps.instruction: Spray‑paint the top ~30 cm of the tank’s interior white (use ventilation).

steps.title: Connect power supply to actuator
steps.instruction: Plug the actuator’s cord into the supplied power supply and connect the power supply to an electrical outlet.

steps.title: Set up visual cues and curtain
steps.instruction: Attach thick poster‑board cues (spray‑painted black) to the walls surrounding the tank. Install a telescoping curtain rod with pole sockets over the door and hang an additional black cardboard cue from the rod.

steps.title: Mount camera and connect to computer
steps.instruction: Mount the industrial monochrome camera with T2Z 1816 CS lens to a ceiling pipe using a clamp mount and flexible gooseneck arm. Connect the camera to a computer outside the room with a USB 2.0 Type‑A cable.

steps.title: Fill tank and position platform
steps.instruction: Fill the tank to ~10 cm below the rim, ensuring the platform surface sits 2 cm below the water surface each testing day.

steps.title: Make water opaque with white acrylic paint
steps.instruction: Add approximately 1 L of white acrylic paint to the water to achieve an opaque color; add more as needed before each testing day.

steps.title: Install and set aquarium heaters
steps.instruction: Clamp three 500 W aquarium heaters to the side of the tank with spring clamps. Set heaters to maximum (water typically stays at 24 °C ± 1 °C). Remove heaters during each trial.

steps.title: Maintain animal body temperature post‑testing
steps.instruction: Immediately after each testing day, use heat lamps to keep the rats warm for ~20 min before returning them to the colony.

steps.title: Remove debris with fish net after trials
steps.instruction: After each trial, use a small aquarium fish net to remove feces and debris from the tank.

steps.title: Conduct Morris water maze testing protocol
steps.instruction: Handle rats for five consecutive days before testing. Mark each rat’s head with a black permanent marker. Run three trials per day for eight days (max 90 s per trial). If a rat fails to find the platform, guide it onto the platform, allow it to rest on the platform for 20 s, then remove it and let it rest an additional 40 s. Every other day, perform a probe trial: lower the platform out of reach, wait 30 s, raise the platform, and continue for up to 60 s or until the rat reaches the platform (guide if needed, then 20 s rest). Use a wireless presentation clicker to start recording as soon as the rat is placed in the tank. One day after the final acquisition day, conduct a visual‑cue session: six 30‑s trials with the platform covered by black drawer liner and visible above the water.
